script: NBA trades where both teams thought they won! In the summer of 2014, LeBron James left Miami and went back home to Cleveland. And the superstar he wanted to team up with was Kevin Love, a three-time All-Star averaging 26 points and 12 rebounds a game for the Minnesota Timberwolves. But actually pulling this trade off got complicated fast. Love had missed the playoffs all six years in Minnesota and already told the team he was leaving, so the Wolves had to move him. Cleveland offered Andrew Wiggins, the number one overall pick that year, along with former number one pick Anthony Bennett and Thaddeus Young came over from Philadelphia in the three-team deal. But there was one weird problem. A rare rule meant the trade couldn't officially happen until thirty days after Wiggins signed his rookie deal, so everyone just had to wait. But the moment it finally went through, both fanbases thought they had just robbed the other one. Cleveland got an A-plus, and Minnesota fans were happy too because they landed two former number one picks to build their future around. So on paper both teams thought they won. Then reality hit, and in 2016 Love helped LeBron win Cleveland its first ever title, with his forgotten defensive stop on Stephen Curry in Game Seven basically sealing it. Meanwhile, none of Minnesota's pieces stuck, and as for Wiggins, he did eventually turn into a steal and win a championship, just not for Minnesota, because he did it for Golden State.
